Cardiology Consultation Note

Reason for Consult:
Palpitations with exertional lightheadedness.

Patient:
Yolanda Pruitt, 55F.

Referring Physician:
Dr. Imani Okafor (Larkspur Family Medicine).

History of Present Illness:
Patient evaluated for exertional palpitations and intermittent lightheadedness. No additional symptom details provided in the record excerpt.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes
- Hyperlipidemia
- Prior tobacco use

Medications / Allergies:
Not provided in the available record excerpt.

Physical Exam (Cardiology):
- General: Not specified.
- Cardiovascular: regular rate; no murmurs; no JVD; no edema.

Diagnostic Studies:
- 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm with frequent PACs.
- Transthoracic echocardiogram (2026-05-29): normal LV size and systolic function (EF 60%); no valvular abnormality; no pericardial effusion.
- Stress test: not yet performed.

Assessment / Impression:
Symptomatic supraventricular ectopy (frequent PACs) with low likelihood of structural heart disease based on recent normal echocardiogram.

Recommendations:
1) Order 14-day ambulatory event monitor to quantify ectopy burden and correlate with symptoms.
2) Start low-dose metoprolol for symptomatic control (dose not specified in source note).
3) Advise limitation of caffeine and other stimulants.
4) Reassess in ~4 weeks after monitor initiation/results.

Follow-up:
Return to cardiology in 4 weeks for review of event monitor and symptom response.

Administrative:
Device-lab scheduling for monitor hookup is currently arranged through the device lab.

Attending Signature:
Attending cardiologist to sign prior to release to the referrer.

Cardiology Consultation Note

Reason for Consult
- Exertional palpitations with lightheadedness.

Patient
- Yolanda Pruitt, 55F.

Referring Physician
- Dr. Imani Okafor (Larkspur Family Medicine).

History (HPI)
- Seen in cardiology for palpitations and associated lightheadedness, particularly with exertion.

Pertinent Past Medical History
- Type 2 diabetes
- Hyperlipidemia
- Prior tobacco use

Medications / Allergies
- Not provided in source data for this draft.

- Cardiac: regular rate, no murmurs, no JVD, no edema.

- Transthoracic echocardiogram (2026-05-29): normal LV size and systolic function (EF 60%); no valvular abnormality; no pericardial effusion.

Assessment / Impression
- Symptomatic supraventricular ectopy (frequent PACs).
- Low likelihood of underlying structural heart disease given normal echocardiogram.

Recommendations / Plan
1. Start low-dose metoprolol for symptomatic PACs (as tolerated).
2. Limit/avoid caffeine and other stimulants.
3. Obtain a 14-day ambulatory event monitor to quantify ectopy burden and assess for any sustained arrhythmia correlating with symptoms.
4. Reassess in ~4 weeks after monitor initiation/results.

Follow-up
- Cardiology follow-up in 4 weeks.

Attending Signature Required
- To be signed by attending cardiologist prior to release to the referrer.

args.content:
Reason for consult: Palpitations evaluation.

History of present illness: 55-year-old female with type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia referred by PCP for exertional palpitations with lightheadedness.

Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes; hyperlipidemia; prior tobacco use.

Physical exam: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs. No JVD. No peripheral edema.

Diagnostic data:
- 12-lead ECG: Sinus rhythm with frequent PACs.
- TTE (2026-05-29): Normal LV size and systolic function (EF 60%); no valvular abnormality; no pericardial effusion.

Assessment/Impression: Symptomatic supraventricular ectopy (frequent PACs). Low likelihood of structural heart disease based on recent normal echocardiogram.

Recommendations:
1) Start low-dose metoprolol (dose per prescribing clinician) for symptom control.
2) 14-day ambulatory event monitor to quantify ectopy/burden and correlate symptoms.
3) Lifestyle: limit caffeine.
4) Follow-up with cardiology in ~4 weeks to review monitor results and symptom response.

Safety/return precautions: Seek urgent care for sustained palpitations with chest pain, syncope, or severe shortness of breath.
